13929: Creation, the fall, the flood and Babel (Gen 1–11). Dates here are not recoverable from the text and are shown only as a span.
13931: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph: the family of promise moves from Ur to Canaan to Egypt (Gen 12–50).
13933: Israel grows in Egypt, is enslaved, and is brought out under Moses; covenant at Sinai and forty years in the wilderness. The exodus date is debated (c. 1446 vs c. 1260 BC).
13935: Joshua leads Israel into Canaan; a cycle of apostasy, oppression and deliverance follows under the judges.
13937: Saul, David and Solomon rule a united Israel; Jerusalem becomes capital and the temple is built.
13939: Israel (north) and Judah (south) split; prophets confront kings. Samaria falls to Assyria in 722 BC; Jerusalem to Babylon in 586 BC.
13941: Judah in Babylon. Daniel and Ezekiel minister among the exiles.
13943: Under Persian rule exiles return, rebuild the temple and walls, and renew the covenant (Ezra, Nehemiah, Haggai, Zechariah, Malachi).
13945: Greek and then Roman rule; Maccabean revolt (167 BC); rise of Pharisees, Sadducees and Essenes.
13947: Birth, ministry, death and resurrection of Jesus of Nazareth (c. 5 BC – AD 30/33).
13949: Pentecost, the spread of the church from Jerusalem to Rome, the letters of the New Testament, and the fall of the temple (AD 70).
13951: Apostolic Fathers, apologists and martyrs; the church grows under intermittent persecution.
13953: From Constantine to Gregory the Great: councils, creeds, Augustine and the Cappadocians.
13955: Monasticism, the East–West schism (1054), scholasticism, penance and purgatory.
13957: Luther, Zwingli, Calvin, the Anabaptists, the Catholic Reformation, Arminius and Dort.
13959: Awakenings, missions, dispensationalism, Pentecostalism and global Christianity.
